- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.4), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a recent spike (e.g., >68.00) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — reduce first 3–5 forecast values by 1–2%.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.5 → -0.3 → +0.4), model fails to capture mean reversion — apply slight downward bias to middle-period forecasts.  
- Model often misses long-term trend (e.g., 10+ day) — if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5–1.5% per day to forecast beyond 10 days.  
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative, model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% for the next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
